correctness.rationale: The actual source RESULT.md (blob 5075f5...) reconstructs the entire extreme-vertex set, including the only orbit coincidence v0=v1 at a=1, and n!/j! orbit multiplicities. Sampling a layer with probability proportional to 1/j! and then a uniform permutation is therefore exactly the uniform distinct-vertex measure. The orbit total S=T_n-D_j and squared norm Q=U_n-A_j yield by permutation invariance C=alpha I+beta 11^T; Var(S)/n and the trace recover the two displayed eigenvalues with correct normalization and multiplicities. Positive weights on distinct layer sums and on nonconstant permutations establish both strict positivities. Factorial tail domination justifies convergence of all needed moments to Poisson(1) or its conditioning J>=1; E[J(J-1)]=1, Var[J(J-1)]=6, and the conditional moment ratio produce the interior and boundary constants. U_n=b^2 n^3/3+O(n^2), T_n=b n^2/2+O(n), so lambda_perp=b^2 n^2/12+O(n), while lambda_parallel=V/n+o(1/n). The source correctly distinguishes fixed a>1 from a=1; no simultaneous parameter/dimension limit is asserted. Independently enumerated distinct vertex sets and exact rational covariance matrices for n=2..5 and parameter pairs (1,1),(2,1),(3,2): all 12 two-eigenvalue formulas matched. These bounded checks are corroboration, not the all-n proof.
risks: The extension to nonintegral a,b uses the explicit orbit-hull definition, not a preexisting combinatorial integer parking-function interpretation.

value.rationale: The eigenstructure of uniform vertices is a natural metric statistic for a canonical generalized permutahedral family whose face and volume enumerations are known. The sharp n^-1 versus n² spectral scales produce cubic anisotropy, and the discontinuity of the vertex measure under a continuous polytope deformation exposes nontrivial geometric/probabilistic behavior. The entire parameter family and asymptotic law supply mathematical content beyond a routine single finite calculation; neither exact enumeration nor novelty alone is the reason for passing.
risks: This does not establish affine-invariant shape or an interior-volume covariance result.

final_claim: For the uniform distribution on distinct vertices of the two-parameter parking-function orbit hull (n>=2, a>=1,b>0), the covariance has exactly the parallel and perpendicular eigenvalues derived from factorial-weighted orbit sums; n*lambda_parallel tends to an explicit positive (conditioned-)Poisson variance, lambda_perp/n^2 to b^2/12, and the ratio is cubic in n, with a strict coalescence jump at a=1.
limitations: The measure is uniform over distinct vertices, not volume-uniform interior; limits fix a and b independently of n.
No claim for general b-vector or mixed n,a->1 regimes.
